measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase Palisade’s town sales tax from 2% to 3%, with the additional tax ending December 31, 2034. It is estimated to raise $600,000 in the first full fiscal year, followed by whatever the tax produces later. The added percentage point would be divided into a 0.75-point share for repairs on 4th, 5th, 6th and 7th streets and improvements to Peach Bowl Park, the swimming pool and Riverbend Park, and a 0.25-point share for emergency services. The town could keep and spend this revenue and investment earnings outside the stated constitutional and other legal limits.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional sales tax through 2034, the specified uses and the revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional tax or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Increase Grand Junction’s sales and use tax from 3.39% to 3.46% beginning January 1, 2027, to repair, renovate and equip the Orchard Mesa swimming pool. The pool could not be expanded beyond its existing six-lane, 25-yard-by-25-meter configuration. The question authorizes $1.9 million in 2027 and whatever the tax produces later. It also authorizes $12 million in borrowing, with total repayment capped at $19 million, paid from this tax or other city general revenue. Part of the increase would end after the debt is repaid, while the remainder would continue for pool operations and maintenance.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the pool tax increase, borrowing and proposed revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this additional pool tax, borrowing or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

parts.label: When the rate would fall
parts.what: A 0.04-percentage-point portion of the increase would end on January 1 after the debt is fully repaid, and no later than December 31, 2047. The remaining 0.03-percentage-point increase would continue to pay for operating and maintaining the pool.

parts.label: Financing and revenue authority
parts.what: The city would set the debt’s sale price and terms, including early repayment with or without an extra charge. The tax could also pay debt principal, any repayment premium, interest and repayment reserves. Tax revenue and investment earnings could be collected and spent outside the stated constitutional and other legal revenue limits.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorize De Beque to charge an occupational tax of up to $5 for each pound of medical marijuana or marijuana products sold or transferred by medical marijuana dispensaries, cultivation businesses or infused-product manufacturers in town, beginning January 1, 2027. The question authorizes $40,000 in the first full fiscal year and whatever the tax produces later. The town could collect and spend this tax revenue outside the constitutional and state-law revenue and spending limits identified in the question.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the proposed medical-marijuana business tax and revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this occupational tax or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Authorize up to $23.2 million in additional school property taxes in 2026 for collection in 2027, through an extra levy starting at no more than 7.850 mills. The rate could increase each year for inflation based on the Denver-Boulder Consumer Price Index. Money would support general school operations, including safety and security staffing, career and technical education, science and technology programs, and teacher and staff pay and benefits. An independent audit would be required each year and published on the district website.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the additional school property tax, inflation adjustment, audit requirement and revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not authorize this additional school property-tax levy or its proposed revenue-limit exception.

parts.label: School-funding limits and revenue
parts.what: This levy would be additional to existing general-fund property taxes. The district could collect the amounts approved by this and earlier local school-tax measures within the combined limit in the cited state school-funding law. It could retain and spend the tax revenue and investment earnings under the proposed constitutional revenue-limit exception.

parts.label: Estimated cost for a home
parts.what: The question estimates an additional $18.09 a month on a $400,000 home using assessed values and assessment rates as of December 2025. The estimate does not include future changes in assessed value, assessment rates or law.

measureRecords.whatItDoes: Raise the district’s general-operating property-tax rate from 5.242 to 11.5 mills beginning January 1, 2027. Together with existing 0.5-mill capital and 0.5-mill pension levies, the total rate would be 12.5 mills. The question authorizes $185,000 annually or the amount raised by the higher rate. Money would support fire prevention and response, emergency medical services, facilities, equipment and other needed property. All revenue from the 12.5-mill levy and other sources could be kept and spent under a permanent exception to the constitutional and state-law revenue and spending limits identified in the question.
measureRecords.yesMeans: Approve the higher fire-district property-tax rate and permanent revenue-limit exception.
measureRecords.noMeans: Do not approve this property-tax rate increase or the proposed permanent revenue-limit exception.

parts.label: Estimated cost for a home
parts.what: The question estimates a 2027 annual tax increase of $42.55 for each $100,000 of residential property value.
